To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) serum levels of IL 10 are lower in patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder when compared to healthy controls; 2) serum levels of TNF a are not different among the three groups; 3) serum levels of the pro inflammatory cytokine IL 6 are significantly increased in patients with schizophrenia when compared to healthy control subjects and patients with bipolar disorder.
serum levels of IL-6, IL-10 and TNF-a were measured in 20 patients with bipolar disorder, 53 with chronic stabilized schizophrenia and 80 healthy subjects.

(i) IL 6 serum levels are increased in schizophrenia patients compared to controls and euthymic BD patients, (ii) IL 10 serum levels are decreased in schizophrenia patients compared with controls, and in bipolar disorder patients compared to controls.

the role of cytokines in the neurobiology of psychiatric disorders.
the study of cytokines in bipolar disorder and their possible role as biomarkers for disease activity or response to treatment.
the role of cytokines in bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia and their possible use as biomarkers of disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

schizophrenia is associated with an increase in pro inflammatory factors and a decrease in anti inflammatory cytokines, while bipolar disorder seems to be related to an episode related increase in IL 6, which may be related to the acute phase of the disease.
the cytokine pattern in bipolar disorder is different than that in schizophrenia.

schizophrenia patients have higher levels of IL 10 and IL 6 than controls, whereas bipolar disorder patients have increased levels of IL 1 6 compared to controls, with no difference in the levels of IL 2 10 between bipolar disorder and controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system is activated in both disorders, but with different patterns of cytokine balance.
the cytokines are not a cause but an effect of disease.
cytokines may play a role in the pathogenesis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is involved in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia.

there is a difference in the pro and anti-inflammatory balance of cytokines in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and that the cytokine profile of schizophrenia may be more consistent and chronic than that of bipolar disorder.
cytokine levels are increased in patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and may play an important role in the pathophysiology of these disorders.
